thread.title: Apple HomePod Goes On Sale, Looks To Put Dent In Smart Speaker Market |

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple HomePod Goes On Sale, Looks To Put Dent In Smart Speaker Market |
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) began taking pre-orders on Friday for HomePod, its voice-controlled music speaker, as the consumer electronics giant makes a late entry in the smart speaker market dominated by Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google.
Apple's HomePod costs $349 and will hit stores on Feb. 9. Apple describes it as a "breakthrough" music speaker with the intelligence of Siri, its voice-response assistant software. It is designed to work with Apple Music, the company's subscription streaming music service, which costs $9.99 a month for an individual plan.
Using Siri on the device, people will be able to use their voice to send a message, set a timer, check the news, sports, traffic and weather, and control HomeKit-enabled smart home accessories.
Apple shares ticked up 0.2% to close at 171.51 on the stock market today .
Apple is positioning its speaker as a high-end audio device to compete with the likes of Sonos, rather than low-cost speakers from Amazon and Google. Amazon Echo speakers start at $49.99 and Google Home speakers start at $49.
In a blog post Tuesday , Sonos knocked the shortcomings of Apple's HomePod. Unlike Apple's device, Sonos speakers use an open platform that allows consumers to use a plethora of streaming music services, including Amazon Music, Apple Music, Google Play Music, Pandora ( P ), Sirius XM ( SIRI ) and Spotify.
The Sonos One speaker, which costs $199, includes Amazon Alexa voice controls and will add Google Assistant voice controls later in the year, Sonos said.
